intent_en: To illustrate how the initial speed of a pandemic's spread determines its severity and outcome, demonstrating that a slower onset keeps infection levels below a critical threshold.
previous_intent: To explain how the initial speed of a pandemic's spread determines its final outcome, contrasting fast spread with a steep infection curve against slow spread with a gentler curve.
narration_support: The question of how pandemics end depends on how they start. If they start fast with a steep slope, they end badly. If they start slow with a not -so -steep slope, they end okayish.
chart_support: Side-by-side line charts plotting Infections against Time for 'Fast Spread' and 'Slow Spread', showing that the fast spread curve has a high peak exceeding a horizontal threshold line while the slow spread curve remains below it.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly states the causal link between start speed (fast/slow) and end outcome (badly/okayish). The chart visualizes this by contrasting a steep, high peak (Fast Spread) with a flat, low peak (Slow Spread) relative to a horizontal capacity line.
